subject: Economy
sub_topic: Types of industries — public, private, joint

concepts.name: Classification of Industries by Ownership: Definitional Boundaries
key_dimensions: Precise definitions of public, private, joint, and cooperative sectors — where one ends and another begins
UPSC trap: Is a company with 51% government stake 'public sector' or 'joint sector'? — threshold ambiguity
Distinction between public sector undertakings (PSUs) and departmental undertakings (Railways, Post)
Role of ownership vs. control in determining sector classification

concepts.name: Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs): Structure and Categories
key_dimensions: Three forms: Departmental Undertakings, Statutory Corporations, Government Companies (under Companies Act)
UPSC trap: Not all PSUs are 'Navratnas' — distinction between Maharatna, Navratna, Miniratna (Category I & II) and their autonomy thresholds
Constitutional backing — Entry 54 (Union List) for nationalization vs. general regulatory powers
Examples and misclassification traps: LIC (statutory), ONGC (government company), Railways (departmental)

concepts.name: Maharatna, Navratna, Miniratna Status: Criteria and Financial Autonomy
key_dimensions: Specific eligibility criteria: Maharatna — net profit ≥ ₹5,000 cr for 3 years, Navratna — composite score of 60/100, Miniratna — profit for 3 consecutive years
UPSC trap: Miniratna Category I can invest up to ₹500 cr without government approval; Category II up to ₹300 cr — exact figures tested
Functional autonomy granted vs. retained government oversight — where the line is drawn
Recent additions/upgrades to these categories as current affairs hooks

concepts.name: Rationale for Public Sector: Historical and Economic Justification
key_dimensions: Industrial Policy Resolution (IPR) 1948 and IPR 1956 — Schedule A (exclusive public sector), Schedule B (mixed), Schedule C (private)
Nehru's 'commanding heights of the economy' doctrine — specific sectors reserved and why
Market failure arguments: natural monopoly, strategic industries, high capital requirement, social equity
UPSC trap: IPR 1956 was aligned with which Five-Year Plan priority? (Second Plan — Mahalanobis model link)

concepts.name: Industrial Policy Resolution 1991: Liberalization and De-reservation
key_dimensions: Reduction of public sector reserved areas from 17 to 8, then to 2 (atomic energy and railways at that time), now effectively 2 — atomic energy and rail operations
UPSC trap: Current status — only Atomic Energy (under Atomic Energy Act 1962) retains full reservation; Indian Railways partially opened
Abolition of industrial licensing (except for specific industries — UPSC often asks 'which ones remain licensed')
Link between 1991 LPG reforms and structural shift in public-private balance

concepts.name: Private Sector Industry: Regulatory Framework and Entry Barriers
key_dimensions: Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951 (IDRA) — scope and current applicability after delicensing
Sectors still requiring industrial licensing post-1991: alcohol, cigarettes, hazardous chemicals, defense equipment, aerospace — UPSC tests the exact list
UPSC trap: FDI sectoral caps and automatic vs. government approval routes — overlap with private sector entry
Competition Act 2002 and CCI's role in regulating private sector dominance — distinction from MRTP Act 1969

concepts.name: Joint Sector Enterprises: Concept, Purpose, and Decline
key_dimensions: Definition: Partnership between government (state/central) and private parties — neither holds 100%
Dutt Committee (1969) recommendation for joint sector as a tool to prevent concentration of private economic power
UPSC trap: Joint sector ≠ Public-Private Partnership (PPP) — key definitional and operational differences
Reasons for decline of joint sector model post-1991 and shift to PPP framework

concepts.name: Public-Private Partnership (PPP) Models: Types and Risk Allocation
key_dimensions: Key PPP models: BOT (Build-Operate-Transfer), BOOT, BOO, DBFOT, HAM (Hybrid Annuity Model) — definitions and differences
UPSC trap: HAM — government pays 40% during construction, 60% as annuity — specific to NHAI road projects; often confused with pure BOT
Risk allocation principle: who bears construction risk, revenue risk, and residual risk in each model
Viability Gap Funding (VGF) — when and why it is used; administered by DEA (Department of Economic Affairs)

concepts.name: Disinvestment vs. Privatization: Conceptual and Policy Distinction
key_dimensions: Disinvestment: government sells minority stake, retains management control; Privatization: transfer of management control to private sector
UPSC trap: Strategic disinvestment = privatization in DIPAM terminology — government deliberately uses 'strategic disinvestment' to avoid political controversy of 'privatization'
DIPAM (Department of Investment and Public Asset Management) vs. earlier DISINVESTMENT Ministry — institutional evolution
National Investment Fund (NIF) — where disinvestment proceeds go and permissible uses

concepts.name: Strategic vs. Non-Strategic Sectors in Disinvestment Policy
key_dimensions: DIPAM/NITI Aayog framework: 4 strategic sectors where government will retain presence — atomic energy/space/defence, transport/telecom, power/petroleum, banking/insurance/financial services
UPSC trap: In non-strategic sectors, government will exit completely — this is the 2021 policy; candidates confuse it with earlier classifications
Air India disinvestment as case study: from non-strategic to completed privatization — process, Tata acquisition
CPSEs identified for closure/merger vs. those for strategic sale — distinction in policy documents

concepts.name: Sick Industries and BIFR/IBC: Institutional Transition
key_dimensions: SICA (Sick Industrial Companies Act) 1985 and BIFR (Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction) — purpose, limitations, and why it failed
Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC) 2016 replacing BIFR — key improvements: time-bound resolution (180+90 days), creditor-in-control model
UPSC trap: BIFR dealt only with companies; IBC covers companies, LLPs, partnerships, and individuals — broader scope
NCLT as adjudicating authority under IBC vs. High Courts under older regime — jurisdictional shift

concepts.name: Small Scale Industries (SSI) / MSMEs: Definition, Classification, and Policy Support
key_dimensions: Revised MSMED Act definition (2020): investment AND turnover criteria — Micro (≤1 cr investment, ≤5 cr turnover), Small (≤10 cr, ≤50 cr), Medium (≤50 cr, ≤250 cr) — exact figures are UPSC traps
UPSC trap: Pre-2020 definition was investment-only based; post-2020 it is composite (investment + turnover) — candidates use old numbers
Udyam Registration Portal replacing Udyog Aadhaar — significance for formalization
Priority Sector Lending (PSL) targets for MSMEs and role of SIDBI as apex institution

concepts.name: Cottage, Small, and Large Industries: Scale-Based Classification
key_dimensions: Cottage industries: family-based, no hired labor, traditional skills (Khadi, handicrafts) — KVIC's role
UPSC trap: Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) is a statutory body under KVIC Act 1956 — not a PSU or ministry department
Ancillary industries definition under MSMED — supplies ≥50% output to a parent unit; policy implications for vendor development
Linkage between cottage/small industry promotion and employment generation vs. efficiency arguments favoring large industries

concepts.name: Industrial Location Theory and Industrial Estates/Clusters
key_dimensions: Weber's least-cost theory (transport cost, labor cost, agglomeration) — applicable in UPSC context for why industries locate near raw materials vs. markets
Industrial clusters policy: MSME clusters, Textile clusters (SCHEME of Fund for Regeneration of Traditional Industries — SFURTI)
UPSC trap: Special Economic Zones (SEZs) vs. Industrial Corridors vs. Export Processing Zones — different regulatory regimes, governing acts
National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation (NICDC) — DMIC, AKIC, CBIC — which corridors exist and their nodal agencies

concepts.name: Special Economic Zones (SEZs): Legal Framework and Controversies
key_dimensions: SEZ Act 2005 — single-window clearance, tax incentives (Section 10AA of Income Tax Act), considered 'deemed foreign territory' for customs
UPSC trap: SEZs are NOT foreign territory for all purposes — currency, criminal law, constitutional rights still apply; only 'deemed foreign territory' for customs/trade purposes
Baba Kalyani Committee (2019) recommendations to convert SEZs into Employment and Economic Enclaves (3Es) — reasons for SEZ underperformance
Comparison with Export Processing Zones (EPZs) — SEZs allow domestic sales (with duty), EPZs did not

concepts.name: Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) in Industry: Sectoral Caps and Routes
key_dimensions: Automatic route vs. Government approval route — who approves under government route (FIPB abolished 2017; now respective ministries + DPIIT coordination)
UPSC trap: FIPB (Foreign Investment Promotion Board) was abolished in 2017 — questions still appear using FIPB as a distractor
Prohibited sectors for FDI: lottery, gambling, chit funds, Nidhi companies, real estate business (not construction), tobacco manufacturing — exact list tested
FDI vs. FPI (Foreign Portfolio Investment) distinction — 10% threshold rule for classification under SEBI/RBI framework

concepts.name: National Manufacturing Policy (NMP) 2011 and Make in India Initiative
key_dimensions: NMP 2011 target: increase manufacturing share to 25% of GDP and create 100 million jobs by 2022 — current status and gap
National Investment and Manufacturing Zones (NIMZs) under NMP — difference from SEZs (NIMZs are greenfield, self-governing industrial townships)
Make in India (2014) — 25 focus sectors, link to PLI (Production Linked Incentive) schemes as the operational tool
UPSC trap: PLI scheme is administered sector-by-sector by respective ministries (not a single nodal ministry) — candidates wrongly assign it to DPIIT alone

concepts.name: Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme: Design and Sector Coverage
key_dimensions: Mechanism: incentive given on incremental sales from a base year — not capital subsidy, not revenue subsidy; output-linked
14 PLI sectors including mobile phones, pharmaceuticals, medical devices, textiles (MMF), white goods, food processing, solar PV, advanced chemistry cells, telecom — UPSC tests sector inclusion
UPSC trap: PLI for textiles covers only man-made fibres (MMF) and technical textiles — NOT cotton textiles; this is a common distractor
Fiscal outlay (₹1.97 lakh crore over 5 years) and expected employment generation — link to Atmanirbhar Bharat narrative

concepts.name: Public Sector Banks vs. Private Banks: Nationalization History and Ownership Overlap
key_dimensions: Bank nationalization: 14 banks in 1969 (banks with deposits >₹50 crore), 6 more in 1980 (deposits >₹200 crore) — specific thresholds are UPSC favorites
UPSC trap: RRBs (Regional Rural Banks) are joint sector — 50% Centre, 15% State, 35% Sponsor Bank — not purely public sector
Small Finance Banks and Payment Banks — RBI licensed, private sector, but serving public purpose — do not confuse with PSBs
Bank privatization debate: Narsimham Committee recommendations vs. current government's selective privatization approach (IDBI Bank case)

concepts.name: Cooperative Sector as a Distinct Category: Constitutional and Institutional Status
key_dimensions: 97th Constitutional Amendment (2011): Article 19(1)(c) amended to include cooperatives; Article 43B (DPSP) added; Part IXB inserted for cooperative societies
UPSC trap: Part IXB applies only to multi-state cooperative societies — single-state cooperatives remain under State List (Entry 32)
New Ministry of Cooperation (2021) — rationale, mandate, and distinction from earlier Department of Agriculture Cooperation
Cooperative sector in specific industries: sugar (Maharashtra, UP), dairy (Amul/GCMMF model), fertilizers (IFFCO, KRIBHCO) — which are multi-state vs. single-state
